note: Mind's-eye coherence test for lyrics. A blind reader (fresh Claude agent; it sees only the lyric, under a neutral filename) says what it pictures. The bar is BlazeDale's (2026-10-17): a listener should be able to piece together a picture that means something to them. It does not have to be the author's intent. one_word records the reader's single-word change suggestion plus Claude's consideration of it. Suggestions are tracked, not applied, unless BlazeDale says so.

readers.v1: PICTURE (2-4 sentences) / VERDICT: ADDS UP or FRAGMENTS / LOOSE LINES. Result: 14 of 14 ADDS UP. Five copies on one lyric (Static) gave near-identical pictures, all hedged with 'maybe a radio, maybe a dead line'. Too charitable to separate songs.
readers.v2: Commit to ONE concrete picture, no hedging / FROM THE LYRIC / INVENTED / MEANING / VERDICT: ADDS UP, THIN or FRAGMENTS / LOOSE LINES / ONE WORD. Result: 15 of 15 ADDS UP, no THIN. The verdict still doesn't separate songs, but INVENTED does: Static's whole visible scene was invented. ONE WORD produced specific, often good fixes.

lyrics.invented: radio set, cabin, night, dial glow, the other went out and was lost: the entire visible scene

one_word.line: Just to know you still can
one_word.why: 'you' could be heard as the absent person; 'I' makes it the speaker proving their own voice
one_word.reason: the double reading is the ache of the song: it can mean you, or the person who can no longer hear

lyrics.invented: the boat's benches, the number of rowers, night, how the hand helps

one_word.why: every other image is water and oars; fire breaks the frame
one_word.reason: keeps the chorus in the boat; two separate readers flagged 'burning'

lyrics.invented: a river seen from midstream, alone, late-winter light

one_word.line: every winter I was told to
one_word.why: the line dangles; 'taught' lets it stand alone as years of learned silence
one_word.reason: both v1 and v2 readers flagged this line as a broken sentence

lyrics.invented: the whole song on one bathroom floor, lying down, late-afternoon sun

one_word.why: 'hometown' points out of the room; 'landmark' keeps the floor as a map
one_word.reason: 'hometown' is the stranger, stronger line: the floor became where they live

lyrics.invented: a country road to a farmhouse, the walker ahead as a stranger

one_word.why: anchors the outro's 'you' to the companion
one_word.reason: verse 2's 'you' is the lost person; 'your' here would merge the two

lyrics.invented: a bed, side by side, the tear catching light

one_word.line: You held it like a bell
one_word.why: a bell is the wrong shape for a tear; pearl matches 'salted moon'
one_word.reason: breaks the fell/bell rhyme, which the reader admits; the image complaint is fair

lyrics.invented: an open field, the note inside the lantern, flame

one_word.line: the weight I've carried, link by link
one_word.why: a chain doesn't belong; 'line by line' ties the weight to the ink
one_word.reason: breaks the ink/link rhyme; but two readers flagged the chain, so the complaint is real

lyrics.invented: a full moon, clear black water, insomnia

one_word.why: love is never set up; faith pays off 'I don't know why it holds'
one_word.reason: the best suggestion of the run: it turns the late-arriving subject into the song's own question

lyrics.invented: night on the singer's side, a parent as caller, a video call, a small rented room

one_word.why: ties the miles to the weak signal
one_word.reason: 'a static sound' sings awkwardly; the line is vague either way

lyrics.invented: porch steps as the place of the call, moths, a window behind the partner

one_word.line: Always an hour from your eyes
one_word.why: one hour can't be sunrise against night across a sea
one_word.reason: fixes a real contradiction that both v1 and v2 readers caught

lyrics.invented: a frozen lake, a tent, a headlamp, the breathing as ice

one_word.reason: the song never names its setting; 'ice' would impose this reader's invented lake on everyone

lyrics.invented: a single blossoming street tree, office workers, a partner

one_word.why: the chorus says 'gone by noon', so starting at midday the blossoms are already gone

lyrics.invented: a farmhouse, an older singer, two neighbours, the breeze

one_word.line: The swallows built up there instead
one_word.why: puts the nest in the broken gate itself
one_word.reason: a minor gain; 'up there' sings more naturally

lyrics.invented: an apartment, a windowsill, a fire escape to the roof, before dawn

one_word.line: I wore the hallway floor to dust
one_word.reason: 'hallway' was my own attractor fix; 'stairwell' does the job better

lyrics.invented: two people, a pack, lying on their back, late afternoon, the country

one_word.why: 'home' was never set up; 'here' stays in the field
one_word.reason: 'home' is the emotional payoff: rest itself is home
